property_summary: balanceOf always reverts when account is the zero address
balanceOf returns zero for any address that has zero balance in the contract after state changes
After calling adjustAdminAccess on an arbitrary address, subsequent balanceOf on that same address returns the same value whether we query before or after the admin access change.
balanceOf always returns a value that is at most the total supply of that token id
After a call to adjustAdminAccess(address,bool), the balanceOf any non-zero address and any token id is 0 before any other operation.
balanceOfBatch returns array where each element matches balanceOf for the given account and id
balanceOfBatch returns balances that are non-zero for accounts that own tokens of the given ids.
balanceOfBatch returns exactly the same values as calling balanceOf individually for each account/id pair
For any account that owns tokens of a given id, balanceOfBatch returns the same value as the individual balanceOf call for that account and id.
For any set of accounts and token IDs, the sum of balances across all accounts for each ID returned by balanceOfBatch matches the sum of balances from individual balanceOf calls.
The balanceOfBatch function returns the same value as balanceOf for the same account and id when queried with a single pair.

The balanceOfBatch function returns an array whose elements are the balances of the corresponding account-id pairs; after adjusting admin access, the property holds that the first element of the returned array equals balanceOf(accounts[0], ids[0]).
The balanceOfBatch function returns an array of the same length as the input accounts array.
balanceOfBatch returns an array whose length equals the number of accounts passed, even after admin access changes.
For any account, token ID pair, after admin access changes, invoking balanceOfBatch with those two arrays always returns the correct balance for each element.
For any caller, after adjusting admin access, calling balanceOfBatch with arrays of length n returns an array of length n.
balanceOfBatch returns an array with elements equal to balanceOf at corresponding accounts and ids indexes, regardless of loop increment prefix.
balanceOfBatch returns an array where each element equals balanceOf of the corresponding account and id, regardless of loop increment type.

The balanceOfBatch function returns an array where the element at any arbitrary index i equals the balanceOf of the same account and id that were passed at that index in the original arrays, regardless of loop increment style.

The balanceOfBatch function returns an array with length equal to accounts.length, and for each index i < accounts.length, the i-th element is the balanceOf of the i-th account and i-th id, irrespective of the loop increment operator.
The balanceOfBatch function returns an array where each element at index i is the balanceOf of accounts[i] and ids[i], regardless of loop increment (++i vs i++).
After calling adjustAdminAccess to revoke admin access, the admin address should no longer be able to call adjustAdminAccess again to restore its own access.
When an owner revokes admin access via adjustAdminAccess, the admin address should not be able to restore its own admin access.
isApprovedForAll returns the same value as the operator approval mapping for the given account and operator.
The isApprovedForAll function returns true for an operator that was previously approved via setApprovalForAll when called with the same account and operator.
The return value of isApprovedForAll should match the stored operator approval for the given account and operator.
The allowanceRemaining for a given owner and tokenId should not increase after a successful mint call.

After a successful mint call, the daily allowance for the caller and tokenId is decremented by the minted quantity, except when the daily allowance replenish time has passed, in which case the allowance is set to the daily allowance minus the quantity.

After a successful mint call, the allowanceRemaining for the caller and tokenId is decremented by the minted quantity, except when the daily allowance replenish time has passed, in which case the allowance is set to the daily allowance minus the quantity.
The allowanceRemaining for a given owner and tokenId decreases or stays the same after a successful mint call.

After a successful mint, allowanceRemaining for the caller and tokenId must equal the previous allowance minus the minted quantity (or the daily allowance minus quantity if allowance was replenished), while the buggy version omits this deduction.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for any address and any tokenId should remain unchanged from its value before the call.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for any address and any tokenId should remain unchanged from its value before the call.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for msg.sender and tokenId 0 remains unchanged if dailyAllowanceReplenishTime is in the future.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for any address and any tokenId should be unchanged, provided the dailyAllowanceReplenishTime is not yet reached.
After adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining for any address and any tokenId with dailyAllowanceReplenishTime in the future is unchanged.
After any interaction ending with adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining[caller][tokenId] should be the greater of its stored value and the token's dailyAllowance if the replenish time has passed.
After any sequence of calls ending with adjustAdminAccess, the allowanceRemaining for the caller on any token should never be less than the dailyAllowance if the replenish time has passed.
After any public calls ending with adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining[caller][tokenId] should be exactly equal to dailyAllowance[tokenId] if the replenish time has passed.
After any call sequence ending with adjustAdminAccess, allowanceRemaining[caller][tokenId] is never set to zero when dailyAllowance is positive and replenish time has passed.
After calling adjustAdminAccess, if the daily allowance replenish time for a token has passed, allowanceRemaining for the caller is at least the token's dailyAllowance.
The dailyAllowanceReplenishTime for the caller is always set to block.timestamp + 1 day after a call to adjustAdminAccess that triggers a replenish.
After any call to adjustAdminAccess, the dailyAllowanceReplenishTime for the caller is at least block.timestamp + 1 day (i.e., not zero or earlier).

After a successful mint where dailyAllowanceReplenishTime <= block.timestamp, the dailyAllowanceReplenishTime for the caller is set to block.timestamp + 1 day (or later) – i.e., it increases by at least 86400 seconds compared to the original value.
After a call to adjustAdminAccess that triggers replenish, the dailyAllowanceReplenishTime for the caller is set to block.timestamp + 1 day.
After a call to adjustAdminAccess, the dailyAllowanceReplenishTime for the caller is never later than block.timestamp + 1 day.
